title: Crunch Time! Zoos Compete to Find the Cutest Chewer
summary:
What's cuter than a fluffy animal nibbling a carrot? How about a whole contest to find the best chewer! Zoos across the United States are sharing adorable videos of tree kangaroos crunching on veggies for the International Tree Kangaroo Crunch-a-Thon. It's all to celebrate World Tree Kangaroo Day on May 21 and to help save these rare animals.

Tree kangaroos are marsupials — that means they carry their babies in pouches, like regular kangaroos. But these guys live in trees! They have long tails, strong arms, and padded feet for climbing. They live in rainforests in Australia, Indonesia, and Papua New Guinea. Some species, like the golden-mantled tree kangaroo, are super endangered and only live in a tiny patch of forest.

The contest is run by a conservation group called AZA SAFE. They asked zoos to post videos on Instagram or Facebook of their tree kangaroos eating crunchy foods like bell peppers, celery, and snap peas. (Cucumbers and zucchini are okay, but they're not as crunchy!) The videos compete for Most Likes, Most Views, and Judges' Choice. Winners will be announced on May 17.

One zoo, the Roger Williams Park Zoo, posted a video of three Matschie's tree kangaroos with pink noses, happily munching away. The organizers say the goal is to "shine a spotlight on this endangered species." So next time you're scrolling online, look for #CrunchAThon — it's a loud, crunchy, and super cute way to help save animals!
why_it_matters: Even a silly video can help save an animal — this shows how you can use social media for good and learn about rare creatures around the world.

background_read: Tree kangaroos are endangered because their rainforest homes are being cut down, and in some places they are hunted.
Papua New Guinea (a country north of Australia) and parts of Indonesia are the main wild homes of tree kangaroos.
AZA SAFE (Saving Animals From Extinction) brings together many zoos to work on conservation projects for species like the tree kangaroo.
Social media contests like this are a new way for zoos to teach people about rare animals and get them excited about helping.
Article_Structure: WHO: Zoos across the United States and the conservation group AZA SAFE
WHAT: They organized the International Tree Kangaroo Crunch-a-Thon, a social media contest where zoos post videos of tree kangaroos eating crunchy vegetables
WHERE: On Instagram and Facebook, with worldwide online voting
WHY: To celebrate World Tree Kangaroo Day on May 21 and shine a spotlight on endangered tree kangaroo species to help save them.

perspectives.description: They believe the contest is a fun, effective way to get people to care about tree kangaroos, leading to more support and donations to protect their habitats.
They are happy because the contest lets them show the animals' natural behaviors and gives the tree kangaroos enrichment through crunchy treats.
Some worry that a short online contest might just be a cute moment, not real conservation action, and that deeper work is needed to save rainforests.
